source.citation: Radi, E., Sevostianov, I. (2016). Toroidal insulating inhomogeneity in an infinite space and related problems. Proceedings of the Royal Society A 472, 20150781.

transcription.from: the figure of the published article (PDF), an embedded image of 384 x 387 pixels: mean ordinate of the colored pixels of each curve at eight abscissas, the axes located on the frame of the plot
transcription.note: Ordinates of the two curves of Fig. 7(a): the components of the temperature flux over the surface of the torus, -k phi_z / (q0 R^3) for a remote flux q0 along the axis (solid line) and -k phi_y / (q0 R^3) for a remote flux across it (dashed line), against lambda = r/R. phi is the integral of T n over the surface of the torus (Eq. 5.1), k the conductivity of the matrix and R the radius of the center line. One pixel is 0.105 on the ordinate and 0.0026 on the abscissa; the lines are 3 to 5 pixels thick. Below lambda = 0.3 the curves are not distinct from the axis at this resolution and are not read. Figures 7(b), 8 and 9 of the article are not transcribed.

reading_uncertainty.description: Uncertainty of an ordinate read on the image: the thickness of the plotted line.
